text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a sudden cluster-wide bump in Xid 13s on a subset of A10 nodes in us-east-1 around 02:10 UTC. Mostly from the search-prod tenant, low-latency small-batch infer workloads. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/gpu-errors :eyes:

gpu-monitor-bot: alert: Xid 13 rate increased 8x on rack-r12 (A10) between 02:08-02:12 UTC. sample_count=124, distinct_cards=6, top_tenant=search-prod

chen: which models are they running? any change push recently?

maria: search-prod using decoder-v2 (seq_len=64 typical), batcher changed to max_batch_size=2 earlier (02:00 UTC) to shave latency. no infra deploy at that time.

priya: interesting — we reduced batching to reduce p99 but that increases PCIe/KV cache churn. could be causing decode kernels to hit a timing window.

oliver: can we grab dmesg and nvidia-smi from one affected host? run `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "2026-03-18 02:00"` and `dmesg | egrep -i "NVRM: Xid|PCIe Bus Error"`

maria: pasted logs from gpunode-12 below:
```
Mar 18 02:09:31 gpunode-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (13): 79, 0c, 00000000, 00000000, 00000000
Mar 18 02:09:31 gpunode-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (13): pcie read error, tag 0x3f
Mar 18 02:09:32 gpunode-12 nvidia: GPU 2: ECC error count incremented: 1
Mar 18 02:09:35 gpunode-12 nv-hostengine: reset start for GPU 2
Mar 18 02:09:36 gpunode-12 nv-hostengine: reset success for GPU 2
```

maria: `nvidia-smi -q` shows GPU 2 reported ECC single-bit and a statistic bump around that minute.

chen: Xid 13 often points to a GPU page fault / ECC event or PCIe error. 79 is interesting — usually decode-heavy workloads with small KV cache touches expose it.

priya: correlating with telemetry: search-prod qps increased 20% at 01:58 UTC (promo traffic), avg batch size dropped to 1.7, observed a spike in context switch rates on infer runners. attaching snippet: `topk(batcher.batch_size, 1m)` shows distribution shifted left.

oliver: do we see any NVLink or power spikes? `ipmitool sensor` looks normal for node. No obvious thermal.

infra-bot: past incidents note: driver 525.85.05 had a handful of Xid 13 reports on A10 under small-batch/high-concurrency loads.

maria: rack-r12 has mixed firmware levels. two GPUs on gpunode-12 are older vbios 90.1, others 92.0. Could be firmware sensitivity.

chen: we should avoid mass reboots. Proposed plan: 1) soft-drain affected GPUs from search-prod via routing rule; 2) collect full kernel+trace logs while reproducing; 3) repro on a sacrificial node with same workload parameters; 4) if repro succeeds, schedule card swap or vbios update during maintenance window.

priya: agreed. we can apply routing change at 02:40 to drain traffic off those cards quickly. I'll add temporary routing rule: `route: search-prod -> exclude rack-r12-gpus[2,5,7]`

oliver: also capture perf counters — run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and enable perfmon on repro node. record PCIe retransmits from `ethtool -S` on host NICs.

maria: quick repro attempt on a repro node (same model + driver): with batch_size=1 and concurrency=24, we reproduced an Xid 13 after ~240s. stack trace attached to the alert (trimmed).

maria: stack snippet:
```
NVRM: Xid (13): 79, pid=4321, pCpfault at 0x7f9a2c... kernel: 0xffffffffc021230
Call trace:
  nvidia_pci_read+0x2a
  nv94_decode_kernel+0x1b4
  nvhost_launch+0xa2
```

chen: that reproduction makes it actionable. Options: downgrade driver to earlier stable, try newer driver candidate, or schedule firmware update. Downgrade risky for other teams.

priya: model-side mitigation: increase max_batch_size to 8 for search-prod temporarily; that'll reduce PCIe churn and likely reduce Xid risk albeit at cost of slightly increased p99. worth it until infra patch.

oliver: I can stage a driver candidate 525.90.01 on staging and run the repro. if it fails there, vendor engagement with NVIDIA is next.

maria: immediate actions agreed: Priya to change batching to 8 for traffic spike window; Chen to apply soft-drain routing; Oliver to run repro with perf counters and try driver candidate; Maria to collect full logs and open an ENG-INFRA incident ticket linking all artifacts.

priya: done — applied batch config change at 02:42 UTC, monitoring p99. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

chen: routing rule applied at 02:43 UTC, search-prod traffic avoiding the 6 suspect GPUs. :white_check_mark:

oliver: started repro job at 02:45, capturing `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi dmon`, `perf` traces. will post results.

maria: note for long term: instrument batcher telemetry to emit PCIe-boundness score (hot KV hits / batch) so we can predict these regression windows. file a small RFC?

chen: agree — also add a policy to auto-soft-drain GPUs that exceed Xid threshold within rolling 5m window to limit blast radius.

maria: taking incident ticket, will ping @eng-oncall if we see >3 distinct cards failing. thanks all. :pray:

gpu-monitor-bot: update: Xid 13 rate back to baseline on rack-r12 after routing and batch change (02:56 UTC). closing alert; follow-up required for driver/firmware plan.
